svg.text: POWER FLOW — WHERE EVERY MEGAWATT COMES FROM
Line thickness is proportional to power. Dashed means idle.
Projected share at full load. Battery covers the ramp, not steady state.
Solar is an input, never a reserve — it can vanish with no warning.
The question is not how full it is — it is how much time it buys.
DISCHARGING — covering the gap while the turbine ramps
FORECAST — THE TWO-STAGE RISE GRIDSIGNAL PREDICTS
Compute reaches full draw in 45 s. Cooling lags 90 s behind it. A reactive system meets each step separately, after it arrives.
GridSignal reads the job scheduler, not the power meter. It knows a 20 MW step is coming
30–60 seconds before it arrives, and stages generation and storage before the load lands.
Every figure below is produced by the running simulator — none is placeholder art.
Predictive horizon — the whole product claim
GridSignal reads the job scheduler's queue, not a power meter. It knows a step-load is
coming 30–60 s before any current flows. Incumbents react after the load has landed.
Not 'battery at 95%'. The operator's real question is how many minutes of cover the
battery buys at the shortfall that is actually predicted. 51 min here.
Turbine ramp rate x lead time vs predicted shortfall. If the battery cannot deliver the
required POWER, this reads INSUFFICIENT even at 95% charge.
Every source is a card with its own state
Colour bar lit = contributing. Grid is greyed because this site is islanded — the
'bring your own power' case that motivates the product.
Flow thickness is proportional to megawatts
Dashed = idle. An investor can read the energy balance in about two seconds without
Load split into IT and cooling
These are two separate events 90 s apart, not one. Cooling lags compute — the
'double whammy' a reactive system meets twice.
Solar is labelled an input, never a reserve. It can vanish with no warning, so it is
subtracted from demand and never counted toward ramp capability.
Available power is 17.0 MW, not 18.0 — one megawatt is withheld because this unit is
the island's grid-forming anchor and must regulate in both directions.
The two-stage rise, forecast before it happens
Compute reaches full draw at 45 s. Cooling settles at ~135 s. This shape is the
product's signature and the reason a single reactive threshold cannot work.
Nine seeded scenarios. Every number on this screen traces to a live simulation field —
nothing here is a static comp.
